title: Successful follow-up
description: A reviewed result is acknowledged, a referral is accepted, an encounter and evidence are recorded, and an authorized clinician closes care.

title: Missing patient acknowledgement
description: Simulated message delivery never becomes acknowledgement; closure remains blocked while explicit patient acknowledgement is absent.

title: Referral rejected
description: The receiving provider rejects with a reason. The current owner retains accountability and receives recovery work.

title: Appointment no-show
description: A scheduled appointment marked no-show does not create a completed encounter or closure evidence.

title: Incomplete clinical documentation
description: An encounter without required clinical documentation remains eligible for evidence collection, never verified closure.

title: Missing closure evidence
description: An attempted closure without policy-required evidence fails without changing the active episode.

title: Corrected laboratory report
description: A new source result version preserves prior history and returns affected care to clinical review.

title: Duplicate webhook delivery
description: The same stable source event delivered twice has one episode and one durable downstream effect.

title: Failed ownership transfer
description: A rejected or unaccepted transfer keeps the prior accountable owner and exposes recovery work.

title: Overdue review escalation
description: A synthetic clinician-approved review deadline passes; an escalation is created without automatic triage or closure.

title: Optional communication consent revoked
description: Revocation before dispatch prevents a queued optional simulated message from being delivered. Care remains active.

title: ML provider unavailable
description: An unavailable research model produces a visibly marked fallback or unavailable state; human workflow and escalation still work.

title: Cross-tenant access attempt
description: An actor without a specific organization grant cannot read or mutate the other tenant episode.

title: Unauthorized closure attempt
description: A coordinator, patient or research service cannot approve clinical closure, even with complete evidence.

title: Clinician-approved verified closure
description: Only an authenticated clinician with current review, explicit acknowledgement, accepted referral, completed encounter and required evidence can close.
